chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: Agents and bad routing
summary: A bad agent booked them back and forth along the Pennsylvania Turnpike, and another agent would not take his call.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But I still didn't have couldn't make enough money. Cause we had -- 'cause we had no agent, I mean the right agent -- he would call us up, man -- I should own a piece of the Pennsylvania Turnpike -- many times
the guy would book us from here to Detroit and then from Detroit back to Washington, and then from Washington back to Chicago.
Did you do one-nighters or did you stay in places for awhile.

No, we stayed in places for a week -- two weeks, and he'd book us in Pittsburgh, book us back here, Philadelphia. Back and forth, instead of getting a routine thing so we could go one behind the other. But he had us goin' back and forth, back across that turnpike. While he's sittin' on the phone. It didn't mean a damn thing.
Did you usually have an agent --?

Yeah I had an agent, I used to do some of my own. I made enemies with 'em because I got tired of 'em. They didn't do nothin' they left me -- I'd have trouble at places I worked and I'd call them up, and one guy say "Well man you woke up my son." Now I'm way out -- where was I at -- we were in Pittsburgh I think. And I believe he was in Boston. And there was a whole lotta trouble. So it must have been about ten o'clock -- ten or eleven o'clock. And all he could find to say to me was that I woke his son up.
Now I'm in trouble up to my neck! Oh, man. Agents.
